n: The final oracle (chapters 12–14) begins. It comes from the Creator who stretched out the heavens, founded the earth, and formed the human spirit. Latter-day Saints see much of these chapters fulfilled at the Lord’s Second Coming.

f.w: formeth the spirit of man within him

n: Jerusalem will be like a cup that makes attacking nations stagger as if drunk, when they besiege Judah and Jerusalem.

f.g: A cup that makes one reel — a symbol of God’s judgment.

n: Jerusalem will be like a heavy stone that injures anyone who tries to lift it, even if all nations unite against it.

f.g: A massive stone, perhaps like those used in ancient weightlifting contests.

f.w: all the people of the earth be gathered together against it

n: God will strike the attackers’ horses with panic and blindness and the riders with madness, while watching over Judah.

f.w: I will open mine eyes upon the house of Judah

n: Judah’s leaders will recognize that Jerusalem’s strength comes from the Lord.

f.w: my strength in the LORD of hosts

n: Judah’s leaders will be like a firepot in a woodpile or a torch among sheaves, consuming the enemies around them. Jerusalem will stand secure in its place.

f.w: an hearth of fire among the wood

n: The Lord will save the countryside of Judah first, so the royal house and Jerusalem don’t boast over the rest. God guards against pride.

f.g: The villages and countryside, outside the walled city.

n: God will protect Jerusalem so that the weakest will be as strong as David, and David’s house like God, like the angel of the Lord leading them.

f.w: he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David
as the angel of the LORD before them

n: On that day God will destroy all the nations that attack Jerusalem.

f.w: I will seek to destroy all the nations

n: A profound prophecy: God will pour out a spirit of grace and prayer, and Jerusalem “shall look upon me whom they have pierced,” mourning as for an only child. John saw this fulfilled at the cross, and the D&C describes Jews recognizing Jesus at His coming.

f.w: they shall look upon me whom they have pierced
the spirit of grace and of supplications
as one mourneth for his only son

n: The mourning will be like the national grief at Megiddo — perhaps recalling the death of good King Josiah there.

f.g: A place near Megiddo; or possibly a pagan mourning ritual.

n: Every family will mourn separately, men and women apart — the royal family of David and of his son Nathan.
The priestly family of Levi and of his grandson Shimei will mourn too. Royal and priestly lines alike repent.
All the remaining families will mourn privately. Real repentance is personal, not just a public show.

f.g: Each in private — deep, individual sorrow.
